changes.reason: Fact History compares full effective timestamps and validates known-time cutoffs at the receipt precision supported by PostgreSQL.

kubernetes.reason: Timestamp validation and comparison run in memory without a Kubernetes or Node Host dependency.
constraints: The existing PostgreSQL adapter consumes the same timestamp strings and requires no schema migration.

aws-lambda.reason: Timestamp validation and comparison use no AWS Lambda resources or invocation lifecycle hooks.
constraints: Store configuration and connection lifecycle stay with the application.

cloudflare.reason: Timestamp validation and comparison use no Workers bindings, persistent storage or Node Container lifecycle hooks.
constraints: This review records the comparison logic and makes no provider support claim.

changes.reason: History reads use the receipt instant and precision of the PostgreSQL column that enforces the cutoff.

kubernetes.reason: Reuse the existing Node PostgreSQL store with an application-supplied pool.
constraints: The application owns connection pooling and the existing Fact History tables.

aws-lambda.reason: Reuse the existing PostgreSQL adapter with an application-supplied connection.
constraints: The application owns connection lifecycle within the invocation and must apply the existing Fact History migration ahead of traffic.

cloudflare.reason: The catalog declares Node and Lambda for the existing node-postgres adapter.
constraints: This change does not add a Workers provider or a Node Container Profile.

changes.reason: Fact History comparisons preserve the original known-time cutoff when collecting source rows.

kubernetes.reason: Cutoff selection is in-memory and has no Kubernetes Node Host capability, storage, or lifecycle requirement.
constraints: The existing Fact History service remains responsible for authorization and storage.

aws-lambda.reason: Cutoff selection is in-memory and has no Lambda Host capability, storage, or lifecycle requirement.
constraints: The existing Fact History service remains responsible for authorization and storage.

cloudflare.reason: Cutoff selection is in-memory and has no Workers or Node Container capability, storage, or lifecycle requirement.
constraints: The existing Fact History service remains responsible for authorization and storage.
